answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing repeated tasks that counterparties verify and by staking a bond that is forfeited when fraud is proven. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one reputation across a terrace of accounts does not multiply trust; each account must separately spend time building a record and lock capital at risk. A garden of linked identities still faces the same verification costs, while a falcon attacker who tries to fake attestations risks losing the bonds that made its accounts credible.
